Background As one of the leading suppliers of fuel cell systems and hydrogen infrastructure in the world, Plug Power (Plug) is familiar with the challenges faced by customers in siting and training for hydrogen (H ) fueling stations. These challenges include safety concerns for 2 personnel handling high pressure components, difficulty training operators in high turnover industries like material handling and maintenance costs associated with mishandling of equipment, and also minimizing the loss of hydrogen during transfer. Fuel cell infrastructure must exceed the standards and expectations set by gasoline fueling to facilitate more widespread adoption of the technology. Automating the hydrogen fueling process so that fuel dispensing equipment can autonomously mate and efficiently interlock with vehicles in need of refueling offers maximum safety as well as a stronger value proposition for fueling station operators and end users and provides a differentiator versus gasoline fueling or battery charging. Fueling of on-road hydrogen vehicles is also a growing need, however the requirements for such applications are distinct from those of materials handling. For liquid hydrogen solutions, the system should be able to transfer the hydrogen safely and autonomously with minimal evaporation losses. The convenience of automated fueling and automated fueling algorithms for liquid hydrogen would allow drivers and operators to spend their time more effectively on other tasks. Automated fueling also enables the adoption of autonomous vehicles, both in the material handling and passenger vehicle industries, by eliminating the need for human interaction to provide round-the-clock service of the vehicle. 6. Objectives The first program objective is to develop an autonomous H fueling dispenser with a H 2 2 nozzle controlled by a robotic arm for a field-deployable automated Autonomous Guided Vehicle (AGV).
